Bud Development:
Bud development (BBCH 01,03,07,09) Occurs in spring, beginning just before inflorescence emergence. This phase continues for 24 days and concludes shortly after the end of inflorescence emergence, around mid-flowering cite{kurokuraRegulationSeasonalFlowering2013, martinezPhenologicalGrowthStages2019}. Bud development begins with visibly swollen buds that feature elongated bud scales and light-colored patches (BBCH 01). The process progresses as bud scales become lighter and densely covered with hairs (BBCH 03). Bud break is marked by the appearance of green leaf tips (BBCH 07) and continues growing until these tips extend about 5 mm above the bud scales (BBCH 09) cite{meierGrowthStagesMonoand1997}.

Bud break number: Averages 10 to 35 buds per 100 cm shoot length cite{labuschagneSelectionIncreasedBudbreak2003}.
Starch content: Decreases in both fine and coarse roots starting from bud break.
Organic carbon reserves: Decrease from bud break to about 30 days after full bloom (DAFB); the greatest deficit occurs around 20 DAFB when fruit diameter is approximately 12 mm cite{ferreeApplesBotanyProduction2003, p. 424}. - Image

Inflorescence Emergence:
Inflorescence emergence (BBCH 51 - 59) Begins prior to vegetative bud development, lasting for 28 days and concluding before vegetative development ends cite{martinezPhenologicalGrowthStages2019}. From 1969 to 2018, the timing of floral bud swelling and bud burst has advanced by 13.8 and 14.8 days, respectively cite{chituTimingPhenologicalStages2020}. The floral bud development starts with swollen buds that have elongated scales and light-colored patches (BBCH 51). As the buds swell, the scales lighten and grow hairy (BBCH 52). Bud burst occurs with the emergence of green leaf tips and visible flowers (BBCH 53), followed by the pink stage where petals elongate and sepals begin to open (BBCH 57). The stage culminates with most flowers forming a hollow ball (BBCH 59) cite{meierGrowthStagesMonoand1997}. - Image

Flowering:
Flowering (BBCH 60 - 69) Occurs in spring after flower emergence cite{kurokuraRegulationSeasonalFlowering2013, milyaevProfilingPhytohormonesApple2022, verheijMorphologicalPhysiologicalAspects1996}. Flowers bloom in a staggered manner cite{martinezPhenologicalGrowthStages2019}, with the flowering date varying by more than 30 days cite{liebhardMappingQuantitativePhysiological2003}.

The duration lasts for several weeks, and most cultivars flower for about 3 weeks cite{ferreeApplesBotanyProduction2003, p. 539}. In the northern hemisphere, full blooming typically takes place between the second and third week of April cite{martinezPhenologicalGrowthStages2019}. At the start of first flowers opening (BBCH 60), sepals and petals of the flower enlarge and separate to expose the stigmas and stamens. The proportion of open flowers varies widely among trees in the same row, ranging from 40 to 95%. Flower growth temporarily ceases before blooming, resuming after successful pollination and fertilization cite{malladiMolecularPhysiologyFruit2020}.

Cell Count in Flowers: Approximately 3–6 million cells cite{musacchiAppleFruitQuality2018}.
Number of flowers in a Cluster: Average ranges from 5.5 to 5.9 flowers per cluster cite{doganGrowthFruitBearing2024a}.

Fruit Development:
Fruit Development (BBCH 71 - 79) Occurs from summer to autumn cite{kurokuraRegulationSeasonalFlowering2013, moserMADSboxGeneMdDAM12020}, this phase follows fruit set, overlaps with the final stage of flowering, and can last for over 160 days cite{martinezPhenologicalGrowthStages2019}. Fruit experiences the first drop approximately 3-4 weeks after full bloom cite{losadaInfluenceProgamicPhase2013}, and the second drop occurs around 4-6 weeks after flowering (cite{ferreeApplesBotanyProduction2003, arseneaultReviewApplePreharvest2016, losadaInfluenceProgamicPhase2013}. Fruit size increases in an expolinear model, with the first fruit drop occurring when the fruit size reaches up to 20 mm (BBCH 71) due to poor fertilization and strong resource limitation, and the second drop around 40 mm (BBCH 73). This stage is defined to end when the fruit reaches 90% of its full size cite{meierGrowthStagesMonoand1997}. For a detailed metabolic view, refer to Table ref{3.5}. Para-dormancy:
Para-dormancy Begins in late summer cite{moserMADSboxGeneMdDAM12020}. The bud is held back by morphogenic signals produced in a tissue other than the meristem itself -- a subtending leaf, a bud scale, or another bud or apex -- which the earlier literature termed correlative inhibition cite{langEndoParaEcodormancy1987}. The bud stays competent to grow, and resumes growth once the inhibiting organ is removed or its signal ceases cite{langEndoParaEcodormancy1987}.

Flower Initiation:
Flower Initiation Begins in summer cite{wilkieRegulationFloralInitiation2008a} extending into early autumn cite{ferreeApplesBotanyProduction2003} Typically begins around mid-July in the Northern Hemisphere and may occur before or after shoot elongation ceases cite{hankeNoFlowerNo2007}.
The broadening of the shoot apex begins around 40 days after full bloom and may continue to 50 days cite{fosterMorphologicalQuantitativeCharacterization2003}. Doming of the apex peaks around 50 days cite{kotodaFloweringJuvenilityApple2021} and might extend up to 127 days after full bloom cite{fosterMorphologicalQuantitativeCharacterization2003}.
The initiation phase generally lasts between 3-7 weeks, but some studies have observed ow it can last up to three months cite{trompLowerbudFormationPome2000}
The shoot apex undergoes broadening and doming in sequential order cite{hirstRootstockEffectsFlowering1995}. Two prerequisites for floral initiation include reaching a sufficient number of appendages and meeting the minimum duration of the plastochron cite{wilkieRegulationFloralInitiation2008a, zhuEffectTemperatureFlowerbud1997}.

Appendages number: varied from 16 to 20 cite{campoyDormancyTemperateFruit2011}

Plastochron: 7 days is the minimum duration for formation of flower bud cite{verheijMorphologicalPhysiologicalAspects1996}

Bud differentiation:
Bud differentiation Follows the initiation stages, starting in the summer cite{hackettJuvenilityMaturationRejuvenation2011}, continuing through autumn cite{wilkieRegulationFloralInitiation2008a}, and largely completes before the onset of dormancy cite{trompLowerbudFormationPome2000}. Flower bud formation completion time varies, ranging from 15 to 22 weeks after full bloom, with variations up to six weeks across different seasons cite{mcartneySeasonalVariationOnset2001}.
Differentiation rates vary by position on the tree: spur buds develop into floral meristems by late summer, whereas extension shoots may continue developing throughout autumn and winter, and possibly into the following spring cite{riveroFloweringPhenologyInterrelations2017} - Apical meristem transitions into an inflorescent meristem and subsequently into floral meristems. cite{malladiMolecularPhysiologyFruit2020}. Initially, the domed apical meristem initiates four to six lateral meristems and bracts. This is followed by terminal flower-initiated bracts and bracelet; lateral floral meristems initiate bracts. Finally, proximal and lateral floral meristem formed floral organs such as sepals, petals, stamens and carpels in sequential order cite{fosterMorphologicalQuantitativeCharacterization2003} - Microscopy / bud dissection

Pollination:
Pollination Occurs during overlapping flowering duration between fruit-producing trees and pollinating trees cite{ferreeApplesBotanyProduction2003}. Optimal pollination should occur from the early flowering stage, when approximately 30% of flowers are open, to full flowering when more than 50% of flowers are completely open cite{liuIdentificationPhenologicalGrowth2015}. The compatible pollen produced by the stamens in pollinators is transferred by pollinators (insects, e.g., honeybees) to pollinate the stigmas of tree flowers cite{ferreeApplesBotanyProduction2003, ramirezApplePollinationReview2013, verheijMorphologicalPhysiologicalAspects1996}. - Temperature

Fertilization:
Fertilization The time from pollination to fertilization ranges from 48 hours to 13 days cite{patriciadenneFruitDevelopmentTree1963}. The interval for fertilization, which is the effective pollination period (EPP), varies from 2-9 days depending on cultivar, tree condition, and temperature cite{ferreeApplesBotanyProduction2003}. Pollen grains deposited on the stigma germinate and the growth of pollen tubes reaches the receptive ovule. The nuclei then travel through the pollen tube to unite with the egg cell and polar nuclei, producing the diploid zygote and a triploid nucleus, respectively. In contrast, flowers without fertilization soon abscise cite{ferreeApplesBotanyProduction2003}. - Temperature
- Irradiation
cite{ramirezApplePollinationReview2013}
Fruit set: Fruit set Typically occurs soon after fertilization cite{ferreeApplesBotanyProduction2003}. 7 days after pollination for ‘Golden Delicious’ cite{losadaInfluenceProgamicPhase2013}. When more than 95% of the petals have fallen, this is recorded as the date of fruit set. The fertilized ovary grows along with surrounding receptacle tissues to form the fruit set, indicating the transition from flower to fruit cite{ferreeApplesBotanyProduction2003, malladiMolecularPhysiologyFruit2020}. - Microscopy / bud dissection
